messages:
maya: FYI CI perf run on PR #4821 just failed the microbench thresholds for kernel_selection and kv_cache tests. Failing job: perf/microbench-kernel-selection

perf-bot: [artifact] https://ci.redwood/reports/4821/summary.html -> kernel_select_ms +18.3% vs baseline (threshold 10%), kv_cache_hit_rate -17.9%

liam: ouch. is this the change that switched kernel ranking to prefer fused kernels by default? commit abcdef1 from 2026-03-12?

maya: yeah that merge is the suspect. Quick diff in CI output:
```
baseline kernel_select_ms: 1.20 ms
PR     kernel_select_ms: 1.42 ms (+0.22 ms, +18.3%)
baseline kv_cache_hit_rate: 0.78
PR     kv_cache_hit_rate: 0.64 (-0.14, -17.9%)
```

natalie: kv cache drop worries me more than raw kernel select time. could be a regression in cache key normalization or an extra invalidation step in the new kernel path.

tom: I kicked off a local profile with the microbench harness + flamegraph. early signal: heap of small allocations inside select_kernel() when falling back to non-fused kernels. looks like we rebuild a key on every request now.

raj: I reproduced locally. Bisect points to abcdef1 -> altering kernel selection scoring. Revert of abcdef1 (temporary) makes perf pass locally.

liam: can we narrow the fix? maybe the scoring change introduced a different key format so existing KV keys don't match and we miss cached entries.

maya: hit this in the CI artifacts: cache keys differ by the 'layout_tag' field introduced in abcdef1. Baseline used omitted-tag form; PR includes tag -> miss. Example: keys
old: "kernel:v2:hid=64:seq=512"
new: "kernel:v2:hid=64:seq=512:layout=col32"

natalie: that explains the hit-rate drop. two options: canonicalize to the old key when layout is default, or migrate cache/accept both formats for a rollout window.

perf-bot: perf ci diff: https://ci.redwood/diffs/4821
Summary: 
- kernel_selection: +18.3% (regression)
- kv_cache_hit_rate: -17.9% (regression)

tom: given this is a regression that impacts unit economics for hosted, we should block the rollout. propose temporary revert on master and put a follow-up PR to normalize keys.

raj: posted PR to revert: https://git.redwood/infra/serve/commit/revert-abcdef1 -> trigger re-run.

ci-bot: Revert PR #4824 created by raj. Running CI (perf jobs included). ETA ~12m.

maya: also adding a microtest to assert cache key stability across kernel-selection changes so future merges fail fast if they alter the canonicalization.

liam: good. add a note in the release checklist that kernel-selection changes must include a KV compatibility plan.

natalie: alternative short fix: allow fallback that strips layout= when looking up cache keys if layout==default. smaller surface area than revert. anyone want to own that patch?

raj: I can open that patch after reverting; will add migration/tests.

maya: re-run CI looks green so far on the revert branch (perf jobs passed locally). If master still fails we'll hold rollout.

perf-bot: CI run for revert-4824 -> perf/microbench-kernel-selection: PASS; kv_cache_hit_rate back to baseline within 2%.

liam: great. we should mark abcdef1 as blocked from re-landing until key compatibility is addressed. I'll add a PR label `perf-blocker` and add to the rollout blocker board.

tom: follow-up work list:
- add unit that diffs cache keys for wide/legacy layouts (maya)
- patch to accept legacy keys (raj)
- end-to-end benchmark to verify no allocation spikes in select_kernel (tom)
- update release checklist + perf sign-off (liam)

maya: thanks all. short postmortem note in #eng-releases and mark this as a rollback-justified perf regression.

raj: filing a short issue with reproducer and flamegraph links: https://issues.redwood/ENG-PRF-2026-17

natalie: please ping me once the migration patch lands; I'll coordinate Dedicated rollout windows. :thumbsup:

maya: closing loop here — master rolled back, follow-ups assigned. We'll re-run the full perf harness after patches.
